summary: My v4 advisory is repaired in the exact construction I proposed: the closed status word is gone, and CA-2 now reads 'This contract does not amend doctor v4. Within the host-effect authorization domain it governs, the declared-local-only branch of doctor v4 consentDoesNotCascade.theHardCase does not make a preview CA-2 exercisable. A later doctor successor may restate that recital.' Every axis the prompt names comes back clean, and the first one deserves particular note because it was aimed at my own v4 verification: I checked key-set bijection last round, and value-totality is now stated as a rule — 'Key-set equality is necessary and not sufficient' — and backed structurally, with actionClass and resolution carrying per-value destinations rather than one string. I re-tested the mapping at both levels and it holds: 19/19 members, no orphan keys, no null or placeholder values, no duplicate destination path. endpointSet and the actual contacted endpoint are now separate fields with conflation failing a named fixture, CA-1 generation and manifest binding is explicitly not SPAWN-only, auditIdentity has its own destination, and BLK-1 now says DR-119 'remains necessary and is not sufficient'. One advisory remains, in the new closed scope shape.

findings.claim: The new consentRecordsScopeShape declares generation, admittedManifestDigest and toolIdentity both as members of consentRecords[].scope and as closedMembers of the nested targetIdentity object, giving one value two legal homes in a shape whose stated purpose is closure; and the toolIdentity destination targets the object rather than its child, which does not type-check against the shape.
findings.evidence: consentRecordsScopeShape declares member 'consentRecords[].scope', closed true, additionalMembers 'forbidden', and a flat members array of sixteen entries. Three of those entries — generation, admittedManifestDigest, toolIdentity — are simultaneously named in the closedMembers list of the targetIdentity entry, which is typed object. On a plain reading of the shape, generation is a member of scope; on the reading the mapping uses, it is a member of scope.targetIdentity. The mapping resolves it one way for two of the three: componentGenerationIdentity maps to 'consentRecords[].scope.targetIdentity.generation' and admittedManifestDigest to 'consentRecords[].scope.targetIdentity.admittedManifestDigest', both naming the child segment. The third does not: toolIdentity maps to 'consentRecords[].scope.targetIdentity for CA-2', naming the object itself. Since targetIdentity is type object and toolIdentity is type string with requiredWhen CA-2, that destination writes a string to an object-typed member and skips the child the shape declares for exactly this purpose. I verified the rest of the shape's coverage mechanically and it is otherwise sound: every scope path any destination writes to is declared, with no undeclared writes. Nothing unsafe follows — CA-2 is wholly unexercisable in the preview, so this destination is currently unreachable, and both candidate homes carry the same value. But a closed shape with two legal locations for one value is the defect class this contract polices elsewhere, at scopeMismatch: 'An attempt whose actual resource, tool, endpoint, check, actor, class, subtype, or platform is not exactly the record's bound is unauthorized… Relabeling after the request is accepted cannot change the required authorization.' A shape that permits the same value in two places makes that rule harder to enforce than it needs to be.
findings.proposedFix: Nest the three children rather than listing them flat — move generation, admittedManifestDigest and toolIdentity out of the top-level members array and give their type and requiredWhen inside the targetIdentity entry — so scope has thirteen members and targetIdentity has three. Then correct the toolIdentity destination to 'consentRecords[].scope.targetIdentity.toolIdentity for CA-2', matching the form the other two already use.

verdictNote: ACCEPT-WITH-ADVISORIES. Across five versions this artifact has taken one blocker and five advisories from me and repaired every one at bytes, twice recording the measurement that exposed the error so it could not recur. The first axis this round was aimed at my own v4 verification — I had checked key-set bijection and not value-totality — and the artifact closes that gap with a rule that says key-set equality is not sufficient and with structure that makes the stronger claim checkable. I re-tested it at both levels and could not break it. The single advisory is a nesting choice in the shape added this round: three names appear both as scope members and as children of targetIdentity, and one destination targets the object where its siblings target the child. Nothing unsafe follows, since CA-2 is unexercisable in the preview and both homes carry the same value, but a closed shape with two legal locations for one value sits awkwardly beside this contract's own scopeMismatch rule. That is one path segment and three member moves to fix.
